title: Miniature L-System Plant Growth Diorama
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D miniature diorama featuring L-system procedural plant growth using Three.js.

## Scene Setup
1. Use a dark earthy background color (#1a0f0a). Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 10) looking at the origin.
2. Add ambient light (intensity 0.3, color #ffeedd) and a directional light simulating warm sunlight from position (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.2 and castShadow enabled.
3. Load the model 'ABeautifulGame.glb' using GLTFLoader. Scale it to 0.02 and position it at (0, 0, 0). This serves as the diorama base/table. Enable shadows on all its meshes.
4. Add OrbitControls with damping enabled, min distance 3, max distance 20.

## L-System Plant Generation
Implement an L-system engine with these rules:
- Axiom: 'F'
- Rules: { 'F': 'FF+[+F-F-F]-[-F+F+F]' }
- Angle: 25 degrees
- Each 'F' draws a cylinder segment (radius 0.02-0.05 depending on depth, length 0.3)
- '[' pushes state (position + rotation), ']' pops state
- '+' rotates +angle around Z, '-' rotates -angle around Z

The plant should grow from a small pot (a brown cylinder, radius 0.3, height 0.4) placed on top of the loaded model at position (0, potTopY, 0) where potTopY is determined by the model's bounding box top.

Plant segments should be colored: trunk segments brown (#5c3a1e), leaf/tip segments green (#2d8a4e). Add small sphere 'buds' (radius 0.04, color #ff6699) at branch tips.

## Growth Animation
- The plant starts at generation 0 (just the axiom, one segment).
- A 'Grow' button (DOM, top-left, id='growBtn') increases the L-system generation by 1, up to max generation 4. Each click regenerates the plant geometry with the new generation string.
- A 'Reset' button (DOM, id='resetBtn') resets to generation 0.
- During growth transition, animate segments appearing over 1 second (scale Y from 0 to 1 per segment, staggered).

## Seasons System
Add a 'Season' button (id='seasonBtn') that cycles through: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter.
- Spring: leaves green (#2d8a4e), buds pink (#ff6699), light warm
- Summer: leaves dark green (#1a6b35), buds yellow (#ffdd00), light bright (intensity 1.5)
- Autumn: leaves orange (#cc6622), buds red (#cc2200), light golden (#ffaa44)
- Winter: leaves removed (transparent/hidden), buds removed, light cool blue (#aabbff), intensity 0.6

## Firefly Particles
Add 20 firefly particles (small glowing spheres, radius 0.03) that float around the diorama in gentle sine-wave paths. They should glow using emissive material (#ffff44). A checkbox (id='firefliesToggle') toggles their visibility.

## HUD / UI
- Display current generation number in a div (id='genDisplay'): 'Generation: X'
- Display current season in a div (id='seasonDisplay'): 'Season: Spring'
- Display plant segment count in a div (id='segmentDisplay'): 'Segments: X'
- All UI elements positioned at top-left, styled with semi-transparent dark background, white text, font-family monospace.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- modelLoaded: boolean (true when GLB loaded)
- generation: number (0-4)
- maxGeneration: 4
- season: string ('Spring'|'Summer'|'Autumn'|'Winter')
- seasonIndex: number (0-3)
- segmentCount: number (count of cylinder segments in current plant)
- budCount: number (count of bud spheres)
- firefliesVisible: boolean
- firefliesCount: 20
- plantHeight: number (approximate max Y of plant geometry)
- potPlaced: boolean (true when pot is positioned on model)
- animating: boolean (true during growth animation)
- lightIntensity: number (current directional light intensity)

## Keyboard Shortcuts
- Press 'G' to trigger grow (same as Grow button)
- Press 'R' to reset (same as Reset button)
- Press 'S' to cycle season
- Press 'F' to toggle fireflies
physics_constraints: L-system geometry must follow deterministic rules: generation N string length must match expected L-system expansion. Plant segments must not have NaN positions. All plant geometry must be above the pot (Y > pot base). Firefly positions must stay within a bounding sphere of radius 5 from origin.
